page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.large is a general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 480 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, which yields 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2056.0, strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.85 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 14.22 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are limited. The stress-ng multi-core performance is poor, and memory bandwidth tests show poor results for uncached reads at 19.96 GB/sec and writes at 14.37 GB/sec. Passmark memory scores and database operations also fall into the poor and weak categories, respectively.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation but low core count and limited memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and simple web serving. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or heavy LLM inference, as evidenced by weak performance in Geekbench compiling and medium model prompt processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex.large offers a modern DDR5 memory architecture and advanced Intel instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AMX, at a lower resource density, making it a viable option for entry-level general-purpose tasks that do not require high multi-core throughput.
